Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call so procurement can evaluate the commercial path: 

Recap (what we heard)
- BlueArc prefers minimizing vendor onboarding when possible; marketplace purchases are often the path of least resistance for your AP team.
- If marketplace isn’t an option, AP typically requests vendor registration (W9, certificate of insurance, SOC2 attestation) and prefers Net30 PO payments.
- For smaller pilots, your product team sometimes uses corporate card to speed pilots up, but Finance caps card approvals based on annual run rate.

Redwood options
- Marketplace (AWS Marketplace + Azure Marketplace): if you buy through marketplace we can invoice via the marketplace provider and avoid direct vendor setup. Pricing is list but we can discuss marketplace promotion options.
- Direct vendor onboarding: we can accept PO (Net30) after vendor setup; we’ll provide W9, SOC2, proof of insurance.
- Card payments: supported for self-serve purchases and mid-size deals; we typically allow corp card for initial pilots up to an annualized threshold.

Attachments: Redwood_Onboarding_Options.pdf (short checklist of required docs and timelines).

Would you confirm: 1) whether BlueArc would prefer marketplace for this purchase, 2) the AP contact we should send vendor forms to, and 3) any hard constraints (e.g., only ACH, no card at all, preferred invoice email address)?

If helpful I can loop in our Sales Ops (monica.patel@redwood.com) and Account Lead (marcus.lin@redwood.com) to prepare the correct vendor packet.

Best,
Evelyn

Thanks Evelyn — useful summary. A few clarifications from AP side: 

- Marketplace: our preferred route if Redwood is available there. It avoids vendor setup and speeds procurement. Which marketplaces are you in? AWS is essential for us.
- Vendor onboarding: AP requires a W9, COI (insurance), SOC2 Type II or equivalent security attestation, and remit-to details. ACH is preferred for large invoices; card is allowed but we need procurement approval if the annual commitment is > $20k.
- Timing: typical vendor setup takes 5–10 business days once we have docs.

I’ve attached our vendor onboarding instructions for your reference (BlueArc_Vendor_Instructions.pdf). Please send W9 and SOC2 link if available. Also copy our AP lead Tim Lee on the vendor packet.
